items.topic: Tailwind typography plugin for markdown rendering
items.context: Prompt-manager's MarkdownRenderer relies on the @tailwindcss/typography plugin to style headings, code, lists, and tables via the `prose` class. Brand-manager currently does not use this plugin. We can either match prompt-manager exactly (install the plugin and scope it to the markdown wrapper) or write per-element Tailwind classes directly in the ported MarkdownRenderer.

options.label: Install @tailwindcss/typography and scope `prose` to the markdown wrapper
options.rationale: Exact match with prompt-manager's pattern (user's d3 guidance was 'do what prompt-manager does'). Minimal porting work — copy the components and the tailwind.config snippet. Easier to keep markdown styling consistent across scenarios. Scoping the `prose` class to a wrapper prevents affecting non-markdown page content.

options.label: Skip the plugin; style markdown elements via ReactMarkdown component overrides with bespoke Tailwind classes
options.rationale: One fewer dependency. No global tailwind.config change. But diverges from prompt-manager's pattern, requires reimplementing styling for every element type (h1-h6, code, ul, table, etc.), and the end result will visually drift from prompt-manager.

items.freeform: See how other scenarios like git-control-tower do it

items.context: Users will often want to read a rule's documentation while running it, or compare two rules' examples. The UI state model can allow multiple cards open at once or enforce accordion (one-at-a-time) behavior.

options.label: Multiple cards can be expanded independently (Record<ruleId, boolean> state)
options.rationale: Supports side-by-side reading and comparing fix instructions across rules. Matches typical documentation-browser UX. Slightly more vertical scrolling when all five are open, but with only 5 rules that is manageable. Recommended.

options.label: Accordion — only one card expanded at a time
options.rationale: Keeps the page compact and focused on a single rule. Easier to scan the full rule list after closing. But blocks comparing two rules without switching back and forth.

items.topic: Compliance summary display format after 'Scan All Rules'
items.context: After a batch scan, the page shows a summary above the rule list. Need to settle what that summary looks like. The data available is pass/fail per rule (with severity).

options.label: Fraction + color ('4/5 rules passing' — green when all pass, amber on any warning-fail, red on any error-fail)
options.rationale: Simple, immediately readable, aligns with the ScannerPage visual language (colored dots). No arithmetic needed to interpret. Severity-aware coloring keeps error-level violations visually distinct from warnings. Recommended.

options.label: Percentage ('80% compliant') with color scale
options.rationale: Feels quantitative and scoreboard-like. But with 5 rules, each failure is a 20% swing — percentage precision overstates the granularity.

options.label: Letter grade (A/B/C/D/F mapped from pass ratio)
options.rationale: Memorable and at-a-glance. But arbitrary thresholds, implies academic correctness, and doesn't naturally surface severity differences (one error-level failure should feel worse than one info-level failure).

options.label: Severity-weighted score (e.g. errors count 3x, warnings 2x, info 1x)
options.rationale: Captures severity directly in a single number. But the weighting is opinionated and not user-configurable, and the number won't map to anything users already know.

items.text: Confirmed prompt-manager's markdown stack (per d3): react-markdown@^9.1.0, remark-gfm@^4.0.1, marked@^15.0.0, shiki@^1.29.2, plus @tailwindcss/typography. The two files to port are scenarios/prompt-manager/ui/src/components/markdown/MarkdownRenderer.tsx (ReactMarkdown wrapper with custom component overrides) and .../components/CodeBlock.tsx (Shiki-powered code blocks with copy button and language label). MarkedParser.ts is prompt-manager-specific preprocessing and does not need to be ported. Brand-manager's package.json has no markdown deps today, so all four libraries are net-new additions.

Round 1 validation report flagged three gaps in plan.md: a missing 'Rollout/Validation Checklist' section, no greenfield declaration, and no `vrooli scenario restart` final cleanup step. All three are now addressed in the updated plan: greenfield declaration is explicit near the top, §12 is a new Rollout/Validation Checklist, and step 4 of that checklist specifies the restart as an operator action (not an agent action) in accordance with the 'no restart active scenario' guidance.

plan_updates: Updated plan.md to (1) add explicit Greenfield Declaration, (2) add §12 Rollout/Validation Checklist including scenario restart as an operator step, (3) incorporate all round-1 settled decisions (d1 hardcoded metadata, d2 ?rule= query param, d3 port prompt-manager markdown stack, d4 shared scenario input), (4) deepen §8 testing plan with named backend and frontend test cases plus a ScannerPage regression guard, (5) expand §9 risk matrix from 3 rows to 7 with likelihood/impact columns covering shiki bundle size, dep-add policy, ScannerPage regression, markdown HTML sanitization, and tailwind prose scoping, (6) specify exact prompt-manager markdown files/versions to port, and (7) note unresolved round-2 decisions (d5 typography plugin, d6 expand behavior, d7 summary format) in the relevant sections.
